ASSESSMENT METHODOLOGY

CONFIDENTIAL · FOR HIRING REVIEW

Partner Growth Manager · Apty

Prepared 6 August 2026

This page sets out how the candidate was assessed. The page that follows covers her in full. Every point is drawn from a recorded, structured screening call

rather than from a resume.

What the role demands

The brief is a hands-on individual contributor rather than a people manager: partner prospecting owned end to end across North America with the United

States primary, accounts identified and tiered, decision-makers engaged directly, roughly three qualified partner meetings created every week, and clean

context handed to the internal team. Ten dimensions carry that emphasis, weighted to fifty:

Authenticity is scored but carries no points; it sets a floor on the recommendation. AI and enrichment are weighted as a method rather than an outcome. The weighting is our

reading of the brief; tell us if your priorities sit differently and we will recalibrate.

How we assess

Resumes are read against the partner-prospecting screening engine, which weighs described work over tool lists. Those who clear it sit a structured phone

screen: five open questions on a North America outbound motion they owned, a target list built from scratch, a campaign that produced qualified meetings, a

meeting they counted as an opportunity and a partner account pursued, each probed for what they personally researched, wrote, sent and confirmed. Two

practical checks follow: choosing the first twenty firms to approach out of a hundred, and the next step when a US practice head asks for more information. A

tool named without the decision behind it is not evidence of prospecting depth.

Score and recommendation

Select, 35 to 50 — take to the hiring-manager round. Grey, 27 to 34 — worth the same round, with the named areas tested inside it. Reject, below 27 —

unlikely to meet the role's requirements. Grey is not a soft no. Where a profile lands there, the areas still to establish are named rather than general, and for this

candidate there are three, set out overleaf.

CONFIDENTIAL · FOR HIRING REVIEW

Partner Growth Manager · Apty

Prepared 6 August 2026

Sakshi Wandhare

30.00 /50

G R E Y

RECOMMENDATION

Hiring-manager round with focused validation

She runs the outbound motion at her company as the only person in the function, and she reasons about which partners are worth pursuing

from where the partnership earns rather than from list filters. Her clearest campaign evidence sits in the UK and Australia, and the numbers

behind the work are the main thing for the round to settle.

5 years in B2B sales and business development · currently Channel Sales Manager, APPSeCONNECT, an integration platform connecting e-commerce, CRM, ERP

and accounting systems, where she owns partner prospecting end to end · North America roughly half the mix, UK and Europe 30 per cent, Australia and Canada the

balance · Hyderabad · 30-day notice · 7021938171 · wandharesakshi86@gmail.com

Against the brief — account selection, outreach construction and campaign judgment are evidenced, and the reasoning is her own rather than borrowed. Personal

targets, the line she draws around a qualified opportunity, and how her fit test travels to Apty's ecosystem are what the round should establish.

What she brings

For the next round

She owns the outbound motion end to end as the only person in the function: ICP definition, list building, sequencing and the partner conversation. Sales Navigator carries account-based outreach, Instantly the cold email, HeyReach the LinkedIn sequences, Apollo and ZoomInfo the list.

Targets and conversion. Her results arrive as descriptions rather than numbers. A target she carried, and what she delivered against it, would read her pace against Apty's three-a-week measure.

Her ICP is the service provider rather than the end user, and she explains why: a Shopify or SAP Business One implementation partner brings a book of clients who each need integration, so one partner is worth many direct accounts. Given a hundred US firms she screens first for at least one connector in common with the stack, then reads LinkedIn presence, headcount growth and revenue direction, and tiers on project volume, because that is where the partnership pays for both sides. She works a hot list of sixty to reach twenty for individual research, and would rather run ten accounts properly than twenty thinly.

What she counts as qualified. She qualifies ahead of the meeting on stack fit and client need, then closes the rest in a fifteen-minute discovery. The line between a reply, a meeting and a qualified opportunity is worth establishing.

On a US account she went in targeting SAP Business One partners specifically, and found on the call that the firm carried several other stacks, with more than twenty connectors in common by her count. Her technical team is now running demos across those stacks. She frames it as choosing one strategic partner over several transactional ones, and accepts the longer cycle that comes with a larger firm.

How the fit test travels. Her first screen is whether a firm implements something her platform already connects to, which works where the product is a connector catalogue. Apty's fit turns on customer access, implementation capability and service mix. Worth hearing how she would build the equivalent here.

On a Shopify partner campaign she led with the deployment time that ready-built connectors save, referenced a recent post from the account, and asked for nothing. The follow-up offers case studies, demo videos or a live customer reference instead of a calendar link. Three email variants ran alongside it: recent comparable work, resources and reference, and closed-deal proof. Asked what she would do if a US practice head replied asking for more information, she answers the same way: offer a choice of demo, case study or reference rather than send a deck.

From the interview

She checks what a question is reaching for before answering, and says plainly when she is reasoning from her current company rather than in general.

Ahead of December in the UK, where she judged new-account outreach would not land, she changed the population rather than the volume and ran a re-engagement campaign against lost and inactive partner accounts. She reports open rates above fifty per cent and meetings from it.

She separates her own work from her team's without being asked to, naming what the two interns run and what she does herself.

Based on a recorded, structured screening call.

Prepared for Apty
